title: Traffic Heatmap Composer for Staged Orchestration
creator: Ethan Rivera
description:
Goal: Design a compact, interactive 'Traffic Heatmap Composer' that lets engineers and product managers visually author staged rollouts (canary / A/B / phased exposure), preview expected user cohorts, and simulate rollback impact. This feature should live in the Redwood Console's Rollouts workspace and integrate with telemetry overlays (errors, latency, cost) so teams can make informed split decisions without leaving the UI.

Context and motivation:
- Current rollouts flows are list- and slider-based; power users request a spatial view to reason about cohort overlap, traffic concentration, and multi-stage ramping.
- Marketing and SRE teams want a simulation mode showing projected error-rate drift and cost delta for each stage.
- Must remain readable at small canvas sizes (dashboard embed) and accessible (color contrast + patterns).

Scope of this ticket:
1) Low- and high-fidelity prototypes for: canvas composer, stage lanes, cohort bindings, transition preview timeline, and rollback rehearsal panel.
2) Interaction spec for creating staged traffic nodes, linking cohorts, and defining gating conditions (metric thresholds, time windows).
3) Simulation engine mock (non-executable) showing latency/error/cost overlays and expected rollback surface area.
4) Handoff-ready assets and component spec for engineering (tokens, states, aria labels, edge cases).

Design constraints & trade-offs considered:
- Information density vs. discoverability: heatmap packs more info but risks cognitive overload. Approach: progressive disclosure with lane focus + mini-map.
- Real-time telemetry vs. cost of polling: prototype uses a "telemetry snapshot" mode (manual refresh) and a live mode with sampling. Engineering flagged cost concerns for live at scale.
- Color-only encoding is not sufficient for accessibility; added texture patterns for cohort types and high-contrast outlines for selected stages.

Key decisions to validate in usability tests:
- Whether a canvas-first composer or a form-first composer with canvas preview yields faster task completion for typical PM workflows.
- Acceptable defaults for stage ramp durations and auto-quarantine thresholds.
- Microcopy around rollback consequences to avoid accidental mass rollbacks.

Deliverables attached to this ticket:
- Figma prototype: high-fidelity flow + small-screen variants (link below).
- Confluence PRD: rollout goals, telemetry schema, acceptance criteria.
- Component spec: color tokens, ARIA attributes, keyboard flow, and animation timings.
- Usability test script and recorded sessions summary.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype covers create/edit/delete for multi-stage rollouts and demonstrates rollback rehearsal.
- Usability test average success rate >= 80% for composing a 3-stage canary.
- Design handoff includes tokenized styles and a prioritized list of engineering risks and instrumentations.

Next steps:
1) Run 6 moderated usability sessions (target users: platform PMs, SRE, growth PM) by 2026-03-18.
2) Incorporate feedback and ship component spec to ENG-45200 for implementation scoping.
3) Coordinate with Runtime and Telemetry teams to define sampling contract for "live" mode.
